summary.bottom_line: Hold what you have and don't add. Chips open about 1.4% lower, but most of that drop comes from a Korea-specific story, so I expect them to claw some of it back by the close. The rest of the market should drift about flat.
summary.where_we_are: 20:16 SGT / 08:16 ET Monday, US pre-market (open at 21:30 SGT); Singapore closed. No US data today. Next: JOLTS job openings Tue 22:00 SGT, PCE inflation Wed 20:30 SGT, Micron earnings Thu 04:05 SGT, payrolls Fri 20:30 SGT.
summary.macro_attribution: Oil moved most: US crude +3.5% to about $95 after Iran refused to soften its terms for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, which pushed gold down 3% on bets the Fed hikes again. The chip call does not need oil to ease, but a 10-year yield above about 5.22% alongside oil above $97 would break it.
what_happened: Chip stocks are down 1.4% pre-market with 17 of 18 names red (tape). The drop is led by Korean memory makers: Samsung -4.7% and SK Hynix -4.6% (tape).

SK Hynix fell after Bloomberg reported that Solidigm, its US storage subsidiary, may list in the US at up to a $100bn valuation. That raised worries about the group's tangled ownership (Bloomberg, Sep 28). This is a holding-company worry, not a sign that AI chip demand is weakening.
Nvidia is up 1.5% pre-market (tape), the only chip name in the green. So the chipmakers themselves are not selling off.
Crude oil +3.5%, gold -3.2%, fear gauge (VIX) +10% to 16.3 (tape; CNBC, Sep 28). Longer-dated volatility is still calm, so this is nervousness, not panic.
Chips ran +7.4% last week and sit about 8.5% above their 50-day average, on thin Friday volume (0.64x normal). They are stretched, which is the reason not to add.

per_group.semis: Slightly up from here. I expect the chipmakers (Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom) to fill part of the gap while memory (SK Hynix's US-listed shares, SanDisk) lags. Micron's results on Wednesday should also pull buyers back into memory.
per_group.big_tech: Flat. Meta is down 2.5% after a 13% week, while higher oil and rate-hike bets weigh on the others. A chip recovery would help, so I see no edge either way.
per_group.market: Flat. There is no data today and futures are down only 0.4%. That is drift, not a break.
per_group.sg_banks: Flat by Tuesday's close. The index rose 0.5% today with all three banks up and UOB up 1.8% on heavy volume, and I expect a quiet US night to leave them there.

change_my_mind: Chip index back to 568-570 in the first hour: the recovery is working.
Nvidia and AMD turn red while memory steadies: the damage is broader than Korea, so flip chips to down.
Crude above $97 with the 10-year yield above 5.22%: rate-hike pressure is biting, so flip chips to down.
Meta falls past -3%: big tech leans down.
summary.confidence: Low. The chip call bets against a 1.4% gap with an oil shock in play, and this record's chip calls are its weakest.
summary.cant_know: Whether Hormuz talks resume this week (Trump says he expects them) or oil spikes again intraday.
summary.the_call: Roughly flat overall, with a mild recovery in chips. The index was off about 0.4% at the open and should finish near there. The chipmakers led by Nvidia recover the most, Korean-linked memory (SK Hynix, SanDisk) recovers the least, and big tech and Singapore banks barely move.
